metadata.summary: These joint EANO–ESMO recommendations address parenchymal brain metastases arising from solid cancers. They cover prevention, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, including neurosurgery, radiotherapy, systemic therapy and supportive care. They exclude brain metastases from primary brain tumours, lymphoma and leukaemia, as well as differential diagnosis and comprehensive palliative care guidance.

conditions_covered: BM from cancer of unknown primary tumour (BM-CUP)
HER2-negative luminal or triple-negative breast cancer
target_population: patients with parenchymal brain metastasis from solid cancers
patients with solid cancers at risk of brain metastasis
patients with a history of brain metastasis

prevention: In the NRG CC001 trial, HA-WBRT plus memantine preserved patient-reported quality of life and reduced cognitive decline compared with WBRT plus memantine; the contribution of memantine remains uncertain.

A randomised phase III trial found no lower probability of cognitive decline with PCI using hippocampal avoidance than with standard PCI. Hippocampal sparing is therefore not standard care in this setting.

recognition: Conventional MRI may not reliably distinguish radionecrosis from tumour progression.

management.actions: Bevacizumab is probably the best treatment; the guideline describes it as more active than steroids and states that it probably does not interfere with immunotherapy efficacy.
The combination is usually managed by avoiding concurrent administration.

prevention: Consider this risk when combining systemic treatment with RT.

toxicities.incidence: The rate of pseudoprogression with immunotherapy alone appears to be low.
recognition: Changes after treatment can be difficult to distinguish from tumour progression on conventional MRI.
immunotherapy RANO criteria account for delayed responses and possible tumour regression after apparent initial progression.

toxicities.incidence: The risk is probably not increased in BM patients in general who receive therapeutic doses of LMWH.
prevention: Consider other bleeding risk factors when assessing anticoagulation.

prophylaxis.recommendation: PCI remains recommended despite concerns about toxicity. Hippocampal sparing is not standard care in this setting.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients with limited and extensive-stage SCLC who have a complete response to chemoradiotherapy

prophylaxis.recommendation: Consider trimethoprimesulfamethoxazole prophylaxis when additional immunosuppressive systemic treatment is given.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients receiving steroids for more than a few weeks together with additional immunosuppressive systemic therapy

prophylaxis.recommendation: Give anticonvulsant prophylaxis after a seizure, at least temporarily. For seizure management, levetiracetam, lamotrigine and lacosamide are preferred over phenytoin, carbamazepine or valproic acid because they do not exhibit drug–drug interactions.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients who have experienced a seizure

prophylaxis.recommendation: Do not give primary prophylaxis: effectiveness in preventing a first-ever seizure has not been shown.
Consider primary thromboprophylaxis. LMWH or unfractionated heparin is recommended; when indicated, LMWH should be considered first-line.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients hospitalised for an acute illness or confined to bed

prophylaxis.recommendation: When indicated, consider LMWH as the first-line option.
prophylaxis.target_population: BM patients for whom secondary thromboprophylaxis is indicated

infection_management.prevention: Risk increases with steroid treatment lasting more than a few weeks. Consider trimethoprimesulfamethoxazole prophylaxis if additional immunosuppressive systemic therapy is administered.

therapies_index.name: neurosurgical resection
approved_indications: Consider for a single BM or for multiple resectable BMs.
Consider when the diagnosis or primary tumour is uncertain, more than one tumour is known, the primary tumour rarely causes BM, or a change in molecular profile could affect treatment.
Consider for acute symptoms of raised intracranial pressure; large BMs, particularly those >3 cm diameter; posterior fossa lesions at risk of obstructive hydrocephalus; and cystic or necrotic BMs.
In BM-CUP, resection should be followed by RT to the cavity.
therapies_index.administration: Post-operative MRI should be performed within 48 h to establish the extent of resection.

therapies_index.name: biopsy
approved_indications: Consider when a suspected BM cannot be distinguished with sufficient certainty from a primary brain tumour, abscess or inflammatory lesion.
A diagnostic neurosurgical intervention may be needed when the primary tumour is unknown or the diagnosis or clinically relevant molecular profile is uncertain.

therapies_index.name: cyst aspiration
approved_indications: May be considered before radiosurgery for a cystic BM.

therapies_index.name: laser interstitial thermal therapy
approved_indications: Discussed as an emerging intervention, mainly for recurrent brain tumours and radiation necrosis; its role in BM requires further study.

therapies_index.name: stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS)
approved_indications: Recommended for 1-4 BMs.
May be considered for 5-10 BMs when cumulative tumour volume is <15 ml.
Recommended for the resection cavity after either complete or incomplete BM resection.
therapies_index.administration: Commonly delivered in a single fraction at 15-24 Gy; for larger lesions, lesions near structures at risk or previously irradiated patients, fractionated treatment in two to five fractions is preferred.
key_toxicities: Radiation necrosis may occur after SRT.
monitoring: Brain MRI every 2-3 months or when neurological progression is suspected.

therapies_index.name: stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT)
approved_indications: Used as a local treatment for BM, including after surgery.
Fractionated stereotactic treatment is preferred for lesions >3 cm diameter, lesions close to structures at risk or in previously irradiated patients.
therapies_index.administration: Fractionated SRS is typically delivered as 27 Gy in three fractions or 30 Gy in five fractions; risk-adapted treatment of a larger resection cavity distributes the total dose over three to five fractions.
key_toxicities: Radiation necrosis and other treatment-related changes can complicate assessment after SRT.
monitoring: Brain MRI every 2-3 months or when neurological progression is suspected.

therapies_index.name: whole-brain radiotherapy (WBRT)
approved_indications: Consider for multiple BMs unsuitable for SRS, taking neurological symptoms, lesion characteristics and CNS-active systemic options into account.
Post-operative WBRT after resection or SRS is discouraged.
For patients with multiple BMs unsuitable for SRS and poor PS, supportive care without WBRT should be considered.
therapies_index.administration: Typically 20-30 Gy in 5-10 fractions; the QUARTZ trial used 20 Gy in five fractions.
key_toxicities: Severe dermatitis can occur when WBRT is combined with BRAF inhibitors.
monitoring: Assess cognitive function at baseline and during the course of disease.

therapies_index.name: hippocampal avoiding (HA)-WBRT
approved_indications: Evaluated with memantine in NRG CC001; the trial reported better preservation of patient-reported quality of life and less cognitive decline than with WBRT plus memantine.

therapies_index.name: simultaneous integrated boost
approved_indications: Described as a WBRT-based approach that adds a higher focal dose to visible BMs.
therapies_index.administration: Focal dose escalation is delivered alongside WBRT.

therapies_index.name: prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI)
approved_indications: Still recommended for limited and extensive-stage SCLC after a complete response to chemoradiotherapy.
Its use in extensive-stage SCLC is being challenged because of toxicity and the availability of serial MRI-based follow-up and immune checkpoint inhibition.
key_toxicities: Toxicity, including concern about cognitive decline.
monitoring: Serial MRI-based follow-up is discussed as an alternative approach in extensive-stage SCLC.

therapies_index.name: PCI associated with hippocampal avoidance
approved_indications: Not considered standard care in this setting: a randomised phase III trial found no lower probability of cognitive decline than with standard PCI and no difference in BM incidence at 2 years or survival.
key_toxicities: Cognitive decline was not less likely than with standard PCI in the cited trial.

therapies_index.name: immune checkpoint inhibition
approved_indications: Used as part of systemic treatment for selected patients with NSCLC, SCLC or melanoma BM according to tumour characteristics and clinical status.
monitoring: Treatment response may be assessed with immunotherapy RANO criteria, which account for delayed responses.

therapies_index.name: platinum-based combination chemotherapy
approved_indications: Combined with immune checkpoint inhibition as a standard systemic approach in advanced NSCLC without actionable oncogenic driver alterations.

therapies_index.name: platinum and etoposide combination chemotherapy together with immune checkpoint inhibition
approved_indications: Described as the basis of standard care for extensive SCLC; the additional value of immune checkpoint inhibition specifically for SCLC with BM has not been formally demonstrated.

therapies_index.name: platinum-based chemotherapy
approved_indications: Recommended for patients with SCLC, with or without immune checkpoint inhibition.

therapies_index.name: capecitabine
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM and as a chemotherapy option that may be considered for progressive HER2-negative breast cancer BM after local treatment.

therapies_index.name: cyclophosphamide
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: 5-fluorouracil
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: methotrexate
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: vincristine
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: cisplatin
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: etoposide
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM and as part of combination chemotherapy for extensive SCLC.

therapies_index.name: vinorelbine
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: gemcitabine
approved_indications: Listed among chemotherapy agents used for breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: trastuzumab
approved_indications: Discussed in systemic combinations for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer and BM.

therapies_index.name: lapatinib
approved_indications: Studied with capecitabine for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: lapatinib and capecitabine
approved_indications: Studied in patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer BM who had previously received trastuzumab and were naïve to this combination; evaluated for BM prevention in CEREBEL, which did not demonstrate greater efficacy than trastuzumab plus capecitabine.

therapies_index.name: neratinib
approved_indications: Studied with capecitabine in patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, including patients with BM.

therapies_index.name: neratinib plus capecitabine
approved_indications: Compared with lapatinib plus capecitabine in the second/third-line NALA study; also studied in previously locally treated BM from HER2-positive breast cancer.

therapies_index.name: trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
approved_indications: Evaluated in HER2-positive breast cancer patients previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane, including an EMILIA subgroup with asymptomatic CNS metastases.

therapies_index.name: tucatinib
approved_indications: Studied with capecitabine and trastuzumab in a third-line trial that included patients with HER2-positive breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: tucatinib, capecitabine and trastuzumab
approved_indications: Studied as third-line treatment in HER2CLIMB, including patients with breast cancer BM.

therapies_index.name: trastuzumab and capecitabine
approved_indications: Used as a comparator for patients with HER2-positive breast cancer, including patients with BM.

therapies_index.name: abemaciclib
approved_indications: Studied in heavily pre-treated patients with BM from estrogen receptor-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer.

therapies_index.name: pertuzumab
approved_indications: Studied with trastuzumab and docetaxel for breast cancer in CLEOPATRA, including assessment of time until BM development.

therapies_index.name: trastuzumab and docetaxel
approved_indications: Breast cancer treatment used as the comparator for adding pertuzumab in CLEOPATRA.

therapies_index.name: pertuzumab to trastuzumab and docetaxel
approved_indications: Studied for breast cancer in CLEOPATRA; among patients whose first recurrence was in the brain, adding pertuzumab increased median time to BM from 12 to 15 months.

therapies_index.name: docetaxel
approved_indications: Included in breast cancer combinations evaluated in CLEOPATRA.

therapies_index.name: eribulin
approved_indications: May be considered as standard chemotherapy for progressive HER2-negative breast cancer BM after local treatment.

therapies_index.name: carboplatin
approved_indications: Mentioned with bevacizumab as chemotherapy that may be considered for progressive HER2-negative breast cancer BM after local treatment.

therapies_index.name: carboplatin and bevacizumab
approved_indications: May be considered for progressive HER2-negative breast cancer BM after local treatment.

therapies_index.name: bevacizumab
approved_indications: Mentioned with carboplatin for progressive HER2-negative breast cancer BM after local treatment.
Described as probably the best agent for radiation necrosis after SRT.

therapies_index.name: pembrolizumab
approved_indications: Early evidence suggests activity in untreated NSCLC BM; prospective evidence specifically for asymptomatic BM remains limited.

therapies_index.name: nivolumab
approved_indications: Retrospective evidence concerns NSCLC patients with asymptomatic BM; also studied with ipilimumab for melanoma BM.

therapies_index.name: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs)
approved_indications: A standard component of multimodality treatment for NSCLC with actionable oncogenic driver alterations; upfront systemic targeted therapy is recommended for asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM with alterations such as EGFR or ALK or ROS1 rearrangement.

therapies_index.name: osimertinib
approved_indications: Discussed for NSCLC with activating EGFR mutations; controlled trials are needed to establish whether potent brain-penetrant TKIs can remove the need for early SRS.

therapies_index.name: temozolomide
approved_indications: Mentioned as classical chemotherapy with limited efficacy for melanoma BM.

therapies_index.name: dacarbazine
approved_indications: Mentioned as classical chemotherapy with limited efficacy for melanoma BM.

therapies_index.name: fotemustine
approved_indications: Mentioned as classical chemotherapy with limited efficacy for melanoma BM.

therapies_index.name: vemurafenib
approved_indications: Studied as monotherapy in BRAF-mutated melanoma BM and mentioned in a combination evaluated for asymptomatic untreated BM.
key_toxicities: BRAF inhibitors combined with WBRT can cause severe dermatitis.

therapies_index.name: dabrafenib
approved_indications: Studied as monotherapy in BRAF-mutated melanoma BM; recommended with trametinib for eligible patients with multiple symptomatic BRAF-mutated BMs or requiring 4 mg dexamethasone or more.
key_toxicities: BRAF inhibitors combined with WBRT can cause severe dermatitis.

therapies_index.name: vemurafenib and dabrafenib
approved_indications: The guide describes this combination as having been evaluated in asymptomatic untreated melanoma BM and reports a short overall response duration.
key_toxicities: BRAF inhibitors combined with WBRT can cause severe dermatitis.

therapies_index.name: ipilimumab
approved_indications: Studied with nivolumab in patients with melanoma BM.

therapies_index.name: ipilimumab and nivolumab
approved_indications: Preferred first-line option for asymptomatic melanoma BM in both BRAF wild-type and BRAF-mutated patients; apparent efficacy is lower for symptomatic BM requiring steroids.

therapies_index.name: trametinib
approved_indications: Recommended with dabrafenib for eligible patients with multiple symptomatic BRAF-mutated BMs or requiring 4 mg dexamethasone or more.

therapies_index.name: dabrafenib plus trametinib
approved_indications: Recommended for patients eligible for further treatment who have multiple symptomatic BRAF-mutated BMs or require 4 mg dexamethasone or more.

therapies_index.name: memantine
approved_indications: Evaluated with WBRT in RTOG 0614 and with both WBRT and HA-WBRT in NRG CC001; its contribution to benefit remains unclear.
monitoring: Neurocognitive outcomes were assessed in the cited studies.

therapies_index.name: steroids
approved_indications: Consider only for symptomatic patients when clinically required to control raised intracranial pressure.
therapies_index.administration: Use the lowest dose for the shortest possible time.
key_toxicities: Treatment for more than a few weeks increases the risk of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.
Preliminary evidence suggests an adverse effect on immunotherapy outcomes in patients with BM.
Steroid use is listed among risk factors for thromboembolic events.
monitoring: Assess the need for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis when treatment extends beyond a few weeks and additional immunosuppressive systemic therapy is given.

therapies_index.name: dexamethasone
approved_indications: A requirement for 4 mg dexamethasone or more is a criterion in the recommendation of dabrafenib plus trametinib for eligible patients with BRAF-mutated BM.

therapies_index.name: trimethoprimesulfamethoxazole
approved_indications: Consider for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis when steroids are used for more than a few weeks together with additional immunosuppressive systemic therapy.

therapies_index.name: levetiracetam
approved_indications: Preferred over anticonvulsants with drug interactions for seizure management after a seizure; primary anticonvulsant prophylaxis is not recommended.

therapies_index.name: lamotrigine
approved_indications: Preferred over anticonvulsants with drug interactions for seizure management after a seizure; primary anticonvulsant prophylaxis is not recommended.

therapies_index.name: lacosamide
approved_indications: Preferred over anticonvulsants with drug interactions for seizure management after a seizure; primary anticonvulsant prophylaxis is not recommended.

therapies_index.name: phenytoin
approved_indications: Mentioned as less preferred than anticonvulsants without drug interactions for seizure management.

therapies_index.name: carbamazepine
approved_indications: Mentioned as less preferred than anticonvulsants without drug interactions for seizure management.

therapies_index.name: valproic acid
approved_indications: Mentioned as less preferred than anticonvulsants without drug interactions for seizure management.

therapies_index.name: low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH)
approved_indications: Recommended for primary thromboprophylaxis and treatment of VTE; if indicated, it should be considered first-line for primary or secondary thromboprophylaxis and therapeutic VTE treatment in patients with BM.
therapies_index.administration: Therapeutic doses are discussed, but no specific dose or route is given.
key_toxicities: Other risk factors for bleeding should be considered; the guide states that therapeutic LMWH probably does not increase intracranial bleeding risk in patients with BM in general.

therapies_index.name: unfractionated heparin
approved_indications: Recommended for primary thromboprophylaxis and treatment of VTE in patients with BM.

therapies_index.name: direct oral anticoagulants
approved_indications: The guide notes that data for patients with BM are lacking.

therapies_index.name: supportive care
approved_indications: Consider without WBRT for patients with multiple BMs who are unsuitable for SRS and have poor PS; it was also a treatment arm in QUARTZ.

therapies_index.name: palliative care
approved_indications: Included as an option in the proposed management approaches for patients with BM.

therapies_index.name: palliative surgery
approved_indications: Included as an option at progression or recurrence for large BMs, particularly in the posterior fossa.

recommendations.statement: Consider screening for BM in patients with lung cancer, possibly excluding stage I NSCLC, and in patients with stage IV melanoma; screening may also be considered for metastatic HER2-positive or triple-negative breast cancer.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Detecting asymptomatic BM earlier may affect treatment decisions.
recommendations.source_heading: DIAGNOSIS, PATHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY — Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Use neuroimaging to investigate BM in any patient with cancer who develops signs or symptoms of raised intracranial pressure, seizures or new neurological deficits.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: New neurological findings may have causes other than BM, including effects of cancer treatment.
recommendations.source_heading: DIAGNOSIS, PATHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY — Recommendations

recommendations.statement: For suspected BM, include cranial MRI with pre- and post-contrast T1-weighted, T2-weighted and/or T2-FLAIR, and diffusion-weighted sequences in the diagnostic assessment.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Cranial MRI is the reference method for neuroradiological evaluation of suspected BM.
recommendations.source_heading: DIAGNOSIS, PATHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY — Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Apply local institutional algorithms when performing histopathological and immunohistochemical assessment of BM.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.source_heading: DIAGNOSIS, PATHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY — Recommendations

recommendations.statement: When BM is surgically resected, reassess in that lesion the treatment-relevant predictive biomarkers previously identified in the primary tumour or extra-CNS metastasis.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.source_heading: DIAGNOSIS, PATHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY — Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Do not routinely request analyses of cell-free tumour DNA from blood or CSF to characterise or monitor BM.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Liquid biopsies have not yet been incorporated into BM response assessment and follow-up.
recommendations.source_heading: DIAGNOSIS, PATHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY — Recommendations

recommendations.statement: If clinical or neuroimaging findings raise suspicion of leptomeningeal metastasis, perform CSF investigations, including cytology, to rule it out.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.source_heading: DIAGNOSIS, PATHOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY — Recommendations

recommendations.statement: Consider surgery when a brain lesion may not be neoplastic, the primary tumour is unknown, more than one tumour is known, the primary tumour rarely causes BM, or a change in molecular profile from the primary tumour could affect treatment decisions.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Surgical tissue assessment can clarify the diagnosis or identify a clinically relevant molecular change.
recommendations.source_heading: THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES: GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS — Recommendations Surgery

recommendations.statement: Consider surgical resection for a single BM.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: The extent of resection is associated with local BM control.
recommendations.source_heading: THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES: GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS — Recommendations Surgery

recommendations.statement: Surgical resection may be considered when multiple BMs are resectable.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.source_heading: THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES: GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS — Recommendations Surgery

recommendations.statement: Surgery may be considered for patients who need steroids and are candidates for immune checkpoint inhibition.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Resection can permit rapid steroid reduction; preliminary evidence suggests steroid use adversely affects immunotherapy outcomes in patients with BM.
recommendations.source_heading: THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES: GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS — Recommendations Surgery

recommendations.statement: Consider surgery when acute symptoms of raised intracranial pressure occur.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Surgery can provide an immediate therapeutic effect.
recommendations.source_heading: THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES: GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS — Recommendations Surgery

recommendations.statement: Obtain post-operative MRI within 48 h of surgery to establish the extent of resection.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.source_heading: THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES: GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS — Recommendations Surgery

recommendations.statement: Recommend SRS for patients with a limited number of BMs (1-4).
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)

recommendations.statement: SRS may be considered for patients with 5-10 BMs when cumulative tumour volume is <15 ml.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: A prospective study reported similar survival between patients with 2-4 and 5-10 BMs treated with SRS alone.

recommendations.statement: Recommend SRS to the resection cavity following either complete or incomplete BM resection.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: In the cited randomised trial, post-operative SRS significantly improved freedom from local recurrence compared with observation.

recommendations.statement: Discourage post-operative WBRT after neurosurgical resection or after SRS.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Although WBRT improved intracranial control after local treatment of limited BMs, it did not improve OS and adversely affected neurocognitive function.

recommendations.statement: Consider WBRT for multiple BMs unsuitable for SRS, taking account of neurological symptoms, lesion size, number and location, and the selection and availability of CNS-active systemic treatment.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)

recommendations.statement: Consider supportive care without WBRT for patients with multiple BMs who are ineligible for SRS and have poor PS.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: In the QUARTZ trial, median survival was similar with optimal supportive care alone and with its addition to WBRT.

recommendations.statement: Continue to recommend PCI for patients with limited or extensive-stage SCLC who have a complete response to chemoradiotherapy, notwithstanding the stated scepticism about its use.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: The guideline notes that PCI is being challenged in extensive-stage SCLC because of toxicity and the availability of serial MRI-based follow-up and immune checkpoint inhibition.

recommendations.statement: Consider systemic pharmacotherapy for most patients with BMs, selecting it according to the primary tumour’s histological and molecular features and previous treatment.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Drug selection is determined chiefly by tumour histology and molecular characteristics rather than intracranial location.

recommendations.statement: If feasible, consider molecular genetic testing of BM rather than the primary tumour to guide tumour-specific targeted therapy and immunotherapy.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)

recommendations.statement: For patients with HER2-positive breast cancer, asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BMs and preserved general status, consider systemic treatment to defer WBRT.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Targeted systemic treatment can provide intracranial disease control in patients with BM from HER2-positive breast cancer.

recommendations.statement: For HER2-negative breast cancer with BM progressing after local treatment, standard chemotherapy such as capecitabine, eribulin, or carboplatin and bevacizumab may be considered.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)

recommendations.statement: Treat patients with NSCLC lacking actionable oncogenic driver alterations and asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM with upfront immune checkpoint inhibition alone (PD-L1 50%) or systemic chemotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibition (PD-L1 <50%), respectively.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Prospective evidence specifically addressing immunotherapy for asymptomatic BM is limited.

recommendations.statement: Use upfront systemic targeted therapy for patients with NSCLC, asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM, and an actionable oncogenic driver alteration such as EGFR or ALK or ROS1 rearrangement.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: TKIs have produced higher response rates in extracranial and intracranial metastases than classical chemotherapy.

recommendations.statement: Treat patients with SCLC using platinum-based chemotherapy, either without or with immune checkpoint inhibition.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: The added benefit of immune checkpoint inhibition specifically for SCLC patients with BM remains to be formally demonstrated.

recommendations.statement: Prefer first-line ipilimumab combined with nivolumab for asymptomatic patients with BRAF wild-type or BRAF-mutated BM.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Data in asymptomatic BM favour the combination, although trial eligibility selected patients with low CNS tumour burden.

recommendations.statement: Give dabrafenib plus trametinib to patients eligible for further treatment who have multiple symptomatic BRAF-mutated BMs or require 4 mg dexamethasone or more.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: The guideline reports apparently lower efficacy of ipilimumab plus nivolumab in symptomatic patients requiring steroids.

recommendations.statement: Individualise multimodality BM treatment by carefully assessing the respective contributions of surgery, radiation oncology and medical oncology.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Treatment selection depends on clinical and neurological status, comorbidities, imaging, tumour characteristics and previous therapy.

recommendations.statement: Ideally, discuss treatment decisions in a dedicated BM board or disease-specific tumour board involving clinicians experienced in CNS tumour management.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Multimodality treatment requires an individual assessment of the available interventions.

recommendations.statement: Conduct randomised trials in asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM to determine the optimal combination of systemic therapy, including TKI or immune checkpoint inhibition, with surgery or SRS.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Prospective trials have not established the optimal combined-modality approach in this population.

recommendations.statement: Perform a detailed neurological examination every 2-3 months, or sooner if radiological progression is suspected or neurological symptoms or signs arise.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)

recommendations.statement: Assess neurocognitive function and the ability to consent regularly.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)

recommendations.statement: Obtain brain MRI every 2-3 months and whenever neurological progression is suspected.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: MRI is the standard method for BM response assessment and follow-up.

recommendations.statement: Consider advanced MRI methods, including MRS and perfusion imaging, and amino acid PET to help distinguish treatment-related changes from tumour progression.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Conventional MRI does not always reliably separate treatment-related abnormalities from tumour progression.

recommendations.statement: Consider steroids only for symptomatic patients.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: When steroids are clinically required to control raised intracranial pressure, the guideline advises the lowest dose for the shortest feasible period.

recommendations.statement: Do not administer primary anticonvulsant prophylaxis.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: Primary prophylaxis has not been shown to prevent a first seizure.

recommendations.statement: When indicated for patients with BM, consider LMWH first-line for primary or secondary thromboprophylaxis and for treatment of VTE.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)
recommendations.rationale: The guideline states that therapeutic LMWH probably does not increase intracranial bleeding risk in BM patients overall, while other bleeding risks still require consideration.

recommendations.statement: Base decisions about fitness to drive on epilepsy as well as cognitive and other neurological functions, while following applicable national guidelines and law.
recommendations.grading_system: European Federation of Neurological Societies criteria (EANO); adapted Infectious Disease Society of America-United States Public Health Service Grading System (ESMO)

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients whose brain lesion has an uncertain diagnosis, whose primary tumour is unknown, who have more than one known tumour, whose primary tumour rarely causes BM, or for whom a change in molecular profile could affect treatment.
decision_rules: Consider a neurosurgical intervention when establishing the diagnosis or obtaining an updated molecular profile could change management.
Outside emergencies, assess the risks, benefits and required tissue work-up in a multidisciplinary tumour board.

recommended_regimens.name: Surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider surgery to clarify the nature or origin of the lesion or obtain tissue relevant to treatment selection.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: After SRT, biopsy has limited ability to separate progression from treatment effects because active tumour and necrosis can coexist without both being represented in the sample.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a single BM.
decision_rules: Consider resection, particularly when systemic disease is controlled.
Weigh surgery against SRT; an uncertain lesion, a large cystic or necrotic lesion, mass effect, a need for high-dose steroids or a need for molecular profiling favours surgery.

recommended_regimens.name: Surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider surgical resection of a single BM.

recommended_regimens.name: SRS
recommended_regimens.summary: SRS is recommended for a limited number (1-4) of BMs and may be favoured by limited surgical accessibility, greater operative risk or preference for non-invasive outpatient care.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Commonly a single fraction of 15 and 24 Gy.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Extent of resection is associated with local control [EANO: I, A; ESMO: II, A]. En bloc resection may reduce recurrence and leptomeningeal dissemination compared with piecemeal resection.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with multiple resectable BMs, particularly a large lesion (>3 cm diameter) causing raised intracranial pressure or neurological impairment when located in an eloquent brain region, a posterior fossa lesion posing a risk of obstructive hydrocephalus, or a cystic or necrotic lesion.
decision_rules: Multiple resectable BMs may be considered for surgery.
Consider surgery for acute symptoms of raised intracranial pressure.
A cystic or necrotic BM may respond less well to SRT than a solid BM.

recommended_regimens.name: Surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Surgical resection may be considered for multiple resectable BMs.

alternative_regimens.name: cyst aspiration followed by radiosurgery
alternative_regimens.summary: Aspiration before radiosurgery may be considered for a cystic BM.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: For surgery prompted by acute raised intracranial pressure, the grading is [EANO: III, C; ESMO: IV, B]. Surgical resection can facilitate rapid steroid tapering.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients requiring steroids who are candidates for immune checkpoint inhibition.
decision_rules: Surgery may be considered to permit rapid steroid tapering before subsequent treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: Surgery
recommended_regimens.summary: Surgery may be considered in a patient needing steroids who is eligible for immune checkpoint inhibition.

supportive_care: Use the lowest steroid dose for the shortest clinically necessary period when treating raised intracranial pressure.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Preliminary evidence suggests that steroid use adversely affects immunotherapy outcomes in patients with BM.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients after complete or incomplete neurosurgical resection of BM.
decision_rules: Irradiate the resection cavity with SRS after surgery.
For a larger cavity, consider distributing the total dose over three to five fractions rather than giving it in one fraction.

recommended_regimens.name: SRS to the resection cavity
recommended_regimens.summary: SRS to the cavity is recommended after complete or incomplete resection.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the trial by Mahajan et al., freedom from local recurrence was significantly improved with post-operative SRS versus observation. In the trial by Brown et al., OS did not differ between post-operative SRS and WBRT, while cognitive decline occurred more frequently after WBRT.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: For a larger resection cavity, three to five fractions are encouraged.

not_recommended.name: post-operative WBRT
not_recommended.reason: It should be discouraged after neurosurgical resection [EANO: I, A; ESMO: I, E]. WBRT after local treatment improved brain control but not OS and adversely affected neurocognitive function.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a limited number (1-4) of BMs.
decision_rules: Recommend SRS for a limited number of lesions.
Prefer fractionated SRS for a lesion >3 cm diameter, a lesion near an at-risk structure such as the brain stem, or a previously irradiated patient.

recommended_regimens.name: SRS
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat the BMs with SRS.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Single-fraction doses are commonly between 15 and 24 Gy.

recommended_regimens.name: fractionated SRS
recommended_regimens.summary: Prefer fractionation for larger lesions, proximity to structures at risk or prior irradiation.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: Two to five fractions; typically 27 Gy in three fractions or 30 Gy in five fractions.

not_recommended.name: WBRT after SRS
not_recommended.reason: WBRT after SRS should be discouraged [EANO: I, A; ESMO: I, E]; after local treatment it improved brain control but not OS and impaired neurocognitive function.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: SRS and surgery can serve either competing or complementary roles; lesion accessibility, surgical risk and preference for outpatient non-invasive treatment inform the choice.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with a higher number (5-10) of BMs and cumulative tumour volume <15 ml.
decision_rules: SRS may be considered when the cumulative tumour volume is <15 ml despite the higher lesion count.

recommended_regimens.name: SRS
recommended_regimens.summary: SRS may be considered for 5-10 BMs when cumulative tumour volume is <15 ml.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In JLGK0901, survival was 10.8 months in patients with 2-4 versus 5-10 BMs; neurocognitive function assessed by the mini-mental state examination was similar between groups when cumulative tumour volume was <15 ml.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited JLGK0901 findings come from a prospective multicentre study of 1194 patients with 1-10 BMs treated with SRS alone.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with multiple BMs unsuitable for SRS.
decision_rules: Consider WBRT according to neurological symptoms, BM size, number and location, and the choice and availability of CNS-active systemic therapy.
WBRT may retain a role for multiple large unresectable BMs, particularly with a recent cancer diagnosis, younger age or good general PS.

recommended_regimens.name: WBRT
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider WBRT when multiple BMs are not amenable to SRS, with selection based on clinical and treatment factors.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: When WBRT was used as initial treatment for multiple BMs, median survival was 3-6 months and 10%-15% of patients with BM were alive at 1 year.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: For patients with multiple BMs, HA-WBRT plus memantine preserved patient-reported quality of life and prevented cognitive decline relative to WBRT plus memantine in NRG CC001. The contribution of memantine remains unclear.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with multiple BMs, poor PS and ineligibility for SRS.
decision_rules: Consider supportive care without WBRT.

recommended_regimens.name: supportive care
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider supportive care while omitting WBRT in this population.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In QUARTZ, patients with NSCLC ineligible for surgery or SRT had similar median survival of w9 weeks with optimal supportive care alone and with optimal supportive care plus WBRT; quality of life was not significantly lower with supportive care alone.

not_recommended.name: WBRT
not_recommended.reason: The guideline calls for considering its omission in patients with multiple BMs who are ineligible for SRS and have poor PS.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The QUARTZ comparison used WBRT at 20 Gy in five fractions; its findings were reported for patients with NSCLC who were not eligible for surgery or SRT.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with limited or extensive-stage SCLC who have a complete response to chemoradiotherapy.
decision_rules: PCI remains recommended after a complete response, notwithstanding concerns about toxicity and the availability of serial MRI-based follow-up.

recommended_regimens.name: PCI
recommended_regimens.summary: Recommend PCI for eligible patients with limited or extensive-stage SCLC.

not_recommended.name: PCI associated with hippocampal avoidance
not_recommended.reason: Hippocampal sparing is not standard care in this setting: a randomised phase III trial found no lower probability of cognitive decline, no difference in BM incidence at 2 years and no survival difference compared with standard PCI.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The role of PCI in extensive-stage SCLC is being challenged because of toxicity, serial MRI-based follow-up and immune checkpoint inhibition.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Most patients with BM for whom systemic treatment is appropriate.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: Histological and molecular characteristics of the primary tumour or, when feasible, the BM.
decision_rules: Base systemic pharmacotherapy on tumour histology, molecular characteristics and previous treatment.
When feasible, consider molecular genetic work-up of the BM rather than the primary tumour to select targeted therapy or immunotherapy.
If several systemic options exist, consider activity against CNS and extra-CNS disease together with their toxicity profiles.
Individualise the contributions of surgery, radiation oncology and medical oncology, ideally through a dedicated BM or disease-specific tumour board.

recommended_regimens.name: systemic pharmacotherapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider tumour-specific systemic treatment for most patients with BM.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The grading for preferring feasible BM molecular work-up over primary-tumour work-up is [EANO: IV, C; ESMO: IV, B]. The grading for considering CNS and extra-CNS activity and toxicity when choosing among systemic options is [EANO: IV, A; ESMO: IV, B]. Gadolinium contrast uptake does not establish that larger therapeutic molecules penetrate adequately.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM and preserved general status.
decision_rules: Consider systemic therapy to postpone WBRT.

recommended_regimens.name: systemic treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider systemic treatment of asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM to delay WBRT.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline does not identify an optimal schedule for combining systemic treatment and RT in breast cancer.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with preserved neurological status (PS 0-2), no neurosurgical indication, previous trastuzumab treatment and no prior capecitabineelapatinib.
decision_rules: The lapatinib and capecitabine combination is described as a systemic option in this previously treated population; the cited response differs by prior BM irradiation.

recommended_regimens.name: lapatinib and capecitabine
recommended_regimens.summary: The guideline reports use of this combination after trastuzumab in patients without a surgical indication.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Brain response was 38% in patients with pre-irradiated BM and 66% in patients with treatment-naïve BM.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: These response figures are results of the cited studies, not a comparative recommendation between the irradiation groups.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with asymptomatic and stable BM entering second/third-line treatment.
decision_rules: The NALA study compared neratinib plus capecitabine with lapatinib plus capecitabine; the guideline reports its BM intervention outcome without designating a preferred regimen from that comparison.

alternative_regimens.name: neratinib plus capecitabine
alternative_regimens.summary: In NALA, the ‘overall cumulative incidence’ of intervention for BM, mostly RT, was 23% in the neratinib arm versus 29% in the comparator arm (P = 0.04).
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The cited comparison involved second/third-line treatment and 130 patients with asymptomatic, stable BM at study entry.

alternative_regimens.name: lapatinib plus capecitabine
alternative_regimens.summary: This was the NALA comparator, with a 29% ‘overall cumulative incidence’ of intervention for BM versus 23% in the neratinib arm (P = 0.04).
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Second/third-line comparator in the cited study.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with BM previously treated with surgery, RT or both, a stable steroid dose and, predominantly, more than two prior systemic treatment lines.
decision_rules: The guideline reports activity of neratinib and capecitabine in a phase II study of this previously treated population.

recommended_regimens.name: neratinib and capecitabine
recommended_regimens.summary: The combination was studied after local and systemic treatment.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The reported control rate approached 50% (22 partial response, 16 stable disease).

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The reported result comes from a phase II study.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane who have asymptomatic CNS metastases.
decision_rules: The guideline describes a secondary analysis of T-DM1 in this previously treated population.

recommended_regimens.name: trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
recommended_regimens.summary: T-DM1 was evaluated in a secondary analysis of the second-line EMILIA study.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Among retrospectively identified patients with asymptomatic CNS metastases (n = 95), median OS was 26.8 months, n = 45 with T-DM1 versus 12.9 months, n = 50 with lapatinib and capecitabine.

alternative_regimens.name: lapatinib and capecitabine
alternative_regimens.summary: This was the EMILIA comparator in the reported secondary analysis.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: The guideline does not specify circumstances favouring it over T-DM1.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: A separate retrospective analysis of T-DM1 reported a response rate of up to 44% among patients with BM from breast cancer, 92% of whom had received local treatment.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with BM included in the HER2CLIMB third-line trial.
decision_rules: The guideline reports a BM subgroup comparison of tucatinib, capecitabine and trastuzumab against trastuzumab and capecitabine.

recommended_regimens.name: tucatinib, capecitabine and trastuzumab
recommended_regimens.summary: The combination was tested in a third-line phase III trial.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Among the 291 patients with BM in HER2CLIMB, median OS was significantly longer with the tucatinib combination than with trastuzumab and capecitabine (18.1 versus 12.0 months).

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The cited OS comparison is from the trial’s BM subgroup analysis.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients whose BM has progressed after local treatment.
decision_rules: Standard chemotherapy may be considered after intracranial progression following local treatment.

recommended_regimens.name: capecitabine
recommended_regimens.summary: May be considered as standard chemotherapy in this setting.

recommended_regimens.name: eribulin
recommended_regimens.summary: May be considered as standard chemotherapy in this setting.

recommended_regimens.name: carboplatin and bevacizumab
recommended_regimens.summary: May be considered after BM progression following local treatment.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Few studies specifically evaluated systemic treatment for HER2-negative luminal or triple-negative BM.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with NSCLC and asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: No actionable oncogenic driver alterations; PD-L1 positivity (>50%).
decision_rules: Use upfront immune checkpoint inhibition alone for the PD-L1-positive population described in the treatment discussion.

recommended_regimens.name: immune checkpoint inhibition alone
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat eligible patients upfront with immune checkpoint inhibition alone.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The formal recommendation prints the monotherapy threshold as ‘PD-L1 50%’, whereas the treatment discussion states ‘PD-L1 positivity (>50%)’; the document does not clarify the discrepancy. Most immunotherapy trials enrolled patients with treated, controlled BM, limiting prospective evidence for asymptomatic BM. Early pembrolizumab data reported CNS response rates in the range of 30% for untreated NSCLC BM; a pooled analysis reported a 27.3% intracranial response rate among patients with ‘active’ BM (n = 73).

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with NSCLC and asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: No actionable oncogenic driver alterations; PD-L1 <50%.
decision_rules: Give systemic chemotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibition upfront.

recommended_regimens.name: systemic chemotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibition
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat eligible patients upfront with combination systemic treatment.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The treatment discussion describes platinum-based combination chemotherapy with immune checkpoint inhibition as standard care in advanced NSCLC without an actionable driver.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with NSCLC and asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic BM.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: Actionable oncogenic driver alterations such as EGFR or ALK or ROS1 rearrangement.
decision_rules: Treat upfront with systemic targeted therapy.
Do not deliver upfront WBRT in patients with EGFR mutation or ALK translocation, according to the consensus described in the guideline.

recommended_regimens.name: systemic targeted therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Use upfront targeted systemic treatment for eligible patients with an actionable alteration.

not_recommended.name: upfront WBRT
not_recommended.reason: The guideline reports widespread consensus against its upfront use with EGFR mutation or ALK translocation.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Retrospective studies of mainly first-generation EGFR inhibitors suggest better survival with upfront TKI plus SRT than sequential treatment, but controlled trials are needed to establish whether brain-penetrant agents including osimertinib can remove the need for early SRS. Fewer sequencing data are available for ALK translocations.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with SCLC, including extensive disease and patients with BM.
decision_rules: Treat SCLC with platinum-based chemotherapy, without or with immune checkpoint inhibition.
For extensive disease, the treatment discussion describes platinum and etoposide combination chemotherapy together with immune checkpoint inhibition as standard care.
Base the addition and timing of SRS or WBRT for BM on symptoms and disease burden.

recommended_regimens.name: platinum-based chemotherapy without or with immune checkpoint inhibition
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat patients with SCLC using platinum-based chemotherapy, either without or with immune checkpoint inhibition.

recommended_regimens.name: platinum and etoposide combination chemotherapy together with immune checkpoint inhibition
recommended_regimens.summary: Described as standard care for extensive SCLC disease.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Added benefit from immune checkpoint inhibition specifically in SCLC patients with BM has not been formally demonstrated. Replacing WBRT with SRS appears to shorten time to CNS progression without compromising OS.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with asymptomatic BM, including those with BRAF-mutated disease.
decision_rules: Prefer ipilimumab with nivolumab as first-line treatment, including for asymptomatic patients with BRAF-mutated BM.

recommended_regimens.name: ipilimumab and nivolumab
recommended_regimens.summary: The preferred first-line option for asymptomatic BM in both BRAF wild-type and BRAF-mutated melanoma.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the cited trials of asymptomatic BM, the combination had an overall response rate of w50% and PFS of >50% at 18 months.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The trials had stringent entry criteria, yielding asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic groups with low CNS tumour burden. In patients with symptomatic BM requiring steroids, the reported intracranial response rate with the combination was 21%. Classical chemotherapy agents were described as having limited efficacy.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with multiple symptomatic BM or requiring 4 mg dexamethasone or more who remain eligible for further treatment.
decision_rules: Give dabrafenib plus trametinib when the specified symptomatic or steroid-requiring criteria apply.

recommended_regimens.name: dabrafenib plus trametinib
recommended_regimens.summary: Treat eligible patients with multiple symptomatic BRAF-mutated BM or a requirement for 4 mg dexamethasone or more.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: When BRAF inhibitors are combined with WBRT, severe dermatitis is a concern; concomitant treatment is usually avoided.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients whose primary tumour remains unknown after an extensive diagnostic work-up, including PET.
treatment_pathways.biomarker_condition: An actionable driver mutation, if detected, may change the restriction on systemic treatment.
decision_rules: Follow surgical resection with RT to the cavity.
In the absence of other tumour manifestations, do not give tumour-agnostic systemic treatment unless an actionable driver mutation is detected.

recommended_regimens.name: surgical resection followed by RT of the cavity
recommended_regimens.summary: Resect the BM and subsequently irradiate the resection cavity.

not_recommended.name: tumour-agnostic systemic treatment
not_recommended.reason: Do not use it when there are no further tumour manifestations and no actionable driver mutation has been detected.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline states that controlled-trial data are unavailable for this specific scenario.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with BM progression or recurrence confirmed through appropriate imaging or tissue analysis.
decision_rules: Ideally review further treatment in a multidisciplinary board.
Select interventions case by case according to performance status, neurological function, the form of CNS progression and previous treatment.

alternative_regimens.name: Surgery
alternative_regimens.summary: May be considered individually, including for a large recurrent BM or a lesion in the posterior fossa.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider the lesion and patient factors and whether further promising systemic options exist.

alternative_regimens.name: repeat SRS
alternative_regimens.summary: May be considered for recurrent or progressive BM.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Individual assessment after confirmation of progression.

alternative_regimens.name: change of systemic treatment
alternative_regimens.summary: May be considered alone or combined with a local intervention.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Select according to the individual disease and prior treatment.

alternative_regimens.name: WBRT
alternative_regimens.summary: The general management algorithm lists WBRT among options at progression if it has not previously been given.
alternative_regimens.conditions_for_use: Consider previous irradiation and the individual clinical situation.

response_assessment.method: Appropriate imaging examinations or tissue analysis
response_assessment.interpretation: Confirm progression before choosing further treatment.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Laser interstitial thermal therapy has encouraging local-control data in recurrent brain tumours and radiation necrosis, but its role in BM needs further study.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Symptomatic patients with raised intracranial pressure, patients with seizures, or patients requiring thromboprophylaxis or treatment of VTE.
decision_rules: Consider steroids only for symptomatic patients and use the lowest dose for the shortest clinically necessary period.
Give anticonvulsant prophylaxis after a seizure, at least transiently, but do not give primary anticonvulsant prophylaxis.
Consider primary thromboprophylaxis during hospitalisation for acute illness or confinement to bed.

recommended_regimens.name: LMWH
recommended_regimens.summary: If indicated, consider LMWH first line for primary or secondary thromboprophylaxis and treatment of VTE in patients with BM.

supportive_care: After a seizure, levetiracetam, lamotrigine and lacosamide are preferred over phenytoin, carbamazepine or valproic acid to avoid drug–drug interactions.

artifacts.title: Figure 1. Immunohistochemical markers for evaluation of metastatic carcinoma of unknown primary (CUP)
artifacts.description: Step 1: For histology compatible with carcinoma or melanoma, consider the initial staining patterns shown: carcinoma, pan-CK+; SCLC or poorly differentiated carcinoma, pan-CK- or (+); melanoma, pan-CK with the result not fully specified in the figure text. Lymphoma is shown as pan-CK-, Vim+, CD45+, and sarcoma as Pan-CK-, Vim+. Step 2: Use CK7/CK20 as the first level of assessment, adding specific markers when clinical findings or histology suggest an origin for CUP. The figure displays CK7+/CK20-, CK20+/CK7- and CK7(+)/CK20(+) patterns, but its text does not reliably assign every listed origin to a branch. Step 3: Compare the tumour with the listed profiles: NSCLC, TTF1+, Napsin+; breast, GCDFP-15+, GATA-3+, Mammaglobin+; thyroid, TTF1+, Thyroglobulin+; mesothelium, CK5/6+, Calretinin+, Vim+, WT1+; endometrium, CEA-, Vim(+); serous ovarian, PAX8+, WT1+; urothelial/transitional cell, CK5/6+, Uroplakin-II+, p40+, p63+, GATA-3+; prostate, PSA+, PSA-P+, NKX3+; renal cell, PAX8+, RCC+, Vim+, with CD10+ for clear cell; liver, Hep Par1+, arginase-1+; melanoma, S100+, HMB45+, Melan-A+; SCLC, TTF1+, CK7(+), CD56(+), Synaptophysin(+), Chromogranin(+); squamous cell, CK5/6+, CK7(+), HPV+, p40+, p63+, p16+, PAX8(+); endocervix, CEA+, p16+, HPV+, PAX8(+); neuroendocrine, Synaptophysin+, Chromogranin+, CD56+; colorectal, CDX2+; mucinous ovarian, PAX8+, CDX2(+), CK7(+), WT1-; upper GI tract, CDX2+, cadherin 17+; pancreas/bile duct, CDX2+, Ca19-9+, CEA(+). The symbol (+) denotes a tendency toward positivity. These are common profiles rather than definitive rules: exceptions occur, especially in less differentiated tumours, and squamous cell and neuroendocrine metastases may lack markers that establish their tissue of origin. DNA methylation, RNA and microRNA (miRNA) analysis have potential for identifying the origin of CUPs but are not yet part of routine clinical practice.

The favourable group comprises 1-10 BMs, depending on total BM volume, controlled extra-CNS disease, good performance status and expected survival >3 months. Unfavourable factors shown are >10 BMs, uncontrolled extra-CNS disease and expected survival <3 months. Step 3: The treatment approaches displayed include surgery followed by SRS/SRT, SRS/SRT alone, surgery followed by systemic pharmacotherapy and systemic pharmacotherapy; WBRT and systemic pharmacotherapy are also displayed, as is palliative care for an unfavourable situation. Step 4: Follow patients at 3-monthly intervals with neurological examination and imaging. Step 5: At progression or recurrence, use performance status, neurological function, the pattern of CNS progression and prior treatment to consider surgery followed by SRS/SRT, SRS/SRT, systemic pharmacotherapy, WBRT if not previously given, or palliative surgery for large BMs, particularly in the posterior fossa; palliative care is also shown. conditions.name: brain metastasis
conditions.description: The guideline addresses parenchymal brain metastases arising from solid cancers. A single BM denotes one intracranial lesion; a solitary BM is the only metastasis identified anywhere in the body.
conditions.epidemiology: About 75% of BMs occur in the cerebral hemispheres, 21% in the cerebellum and up to 3% in the brain stem. Fewer than half are single, and very few are solitary.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Neurological manifestations commonly develop over weeks. Presentations include headache, seizures, hemiparesis, hemisensory loss, personality change, aphasia, visual disturbance and signs of raised intracranial pressure. Focal findings vary with lesion location. Epilepsy risk probably relates to cortical proximity and tumoural haemorrhage. Haemorrhage or obstructive hydrocephalus can cause rapid deterioration.

diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Pre- and post-contrast T1-weighted, T2-weighted and/or T2-FLAIR, and DWI sequences form the minimum examination. Imaging without and with contrast at at least 1.5-T is the reference neuroradiological assessment. Enhancement may be solid or ring-shaped, with perifocal oedema and frequent involvement of the grey–white matter junction or vascular border zones. No imaging-feature combination identifies BM with absolute certainty.
